_comment: Cross-origin isolation is scoped to the RIG DOCUMENT (/play), not
to '**'. It is the document that needs it — the NAM wasm is a
pthread / SharedArrayBuffer build — and same-origin subresources
need no CORP of their own, so nothing is lost by narrowing it.
The landing at / and /signin.html stay un-isolated: under
require-corp every document in the frame tree must carry its own
compatible COEP, and Firebase's auth helper at /__/auth/iframe
carries none. Hosting serves that path from a reserved namespace
no header rule can touch, so sign-in can only happen on a page
that is not isolated.
The web rig and its sign-in page are no longer deployed at all
(SHIP_RIG in tools/assemble-dist.mjs) and now answer 404; the OAuth
callback is still served but is not a published page. All must stay
out of search, and these rules keep reaching anything already in an
index. noindex, NOT a robots.txt Disallow: a Disallow
stops the crawl, which stops Google ever seeing the noindex, and a
bare URL can then sit in the results indefinitely. robots.txt keeps
allowing these paths ON PURPOSE so the directive below is read.
A header rather than only a <meta> because it also covers the
non-HTML under /play (the wasm, the bundles, the UI art), which a
meta tag cannot reach. The pages carry the meta too, so the
directive survives a move to a host that ignores this file.
The landing's css/js are un-hashed files edited in place, so they
must revalidate; the app's /assets bundles are content-hashed and
the landing's images change under new filenames by convention.
A year, immutable. The convention named just above — new art ships
under a new filename — is what makes that safe, so it is now
load-bearing rather than merely tidy: NEVER change the bytes behind
a name under /assets; ship the new file under a new name and
repoint the markup (maine-film-v2.mp4 was exactly that).
This was a day's max-age, which meant every returning visitor
re-pulled the whole media set — most of what walked this project up
to the Spark plan's 10 GB/month egress cap.
